scope: Current Kaggle CLI pulls for exactly abhinav0370/cha22-agent, nihilisticneuralnet/kaggriculture-population-robust-economy, and prvsiyan/kaggriculture-frontier-the-soil-remembers-rain. Notebook cells and policies were not executed. Embedded source was inspected and independently decoded only from AST literals with standard-library base85, zlib, and lzma.

acquisition.kernel_version: The Kaggle CLI metadata/list/files responses do not expose a numeric notebook version; kernel id_no, lastRunTime, and output creation time are recorded per candidate instead.

safety_audit.archive_handling: Downloaded tar.gz files were opened read-only; every member name was checked for absolute paths and '..' components and every member hash was computed without extraction.
common_findings: All three main.py files contain exec calls over fixed source-code string literals for bundled engine/planner helpers. Those literals are part of the policy and run on import, but no downloaded code was imported or executed during this audit.
No policy network or subprocess API was found.
The shared route payload is a fixed 41-route, 719-action-tape family; no episode-id dispatch was found.

shared_route_payload.structure: The decoded object has 3,982 deduplicated actions, 41 route tapes, 64 ordered two-shop mappings, and 719 callbacks per route.
shared_route_payload.production_geometry: The common tapes are mixed livestock/crop schedules, not independent new trajectories: typical routes buy roughly 6-9 cows, 4-11 sheep, and 0-5 geese, while planting wheat, carrot, strawberry, and melon. Most apparent diversity in these three sources is wrapper behavior around this identical route bank.

interpretation: current-multiroute is structurally distinct and compact; all three investigated sources have only 2.5-3.2% line-sequence similarity to it.
current-master-v53 is another compact generalized lineage; similarity to these sources is 54.8-58.2%, materially below their overlap with the large route-wrapper family.
current-godmode delegates to a large base in the same route family and then adds current-shop sale deferral; comparisons therefore use its base_agent.py, not only its 358-byte entry module.
current-harvest is the larger repeated market-closure lineage. The investigated sources share its route bank and many inherited production/economic layers, even when their final wrappers differ.

novelty_ranking.verdict: Most production-relevant mechanism, but not a new local candidate: its normalized AST is exactly identical to kaggriculture-candidates/2945/main.py after comments and docstrings are removed.
novelty_ranking.use: Use the already-present 2945 candidate if a shop- and market-conditioned livestock substitution stressor is absent from the finalist panel; do not add this repackaging as a second opponent.

novelty_ranking.verdict: Some real opening/late-input geometry changes exist, especially the fixed EarlyCycle extra-wheat opening, but the source remains the same route bank plus a very long inherited wrapper stack and overlaps heavily with current Godmode/Harvest ancestry.
novelty_ranking.use: Only realistic as a wrapper-stack stressor if an external adapter selects ig_agent; lower priority than a genuinely independent route or production family.

novelty_ranking.verdict: The final advertised change is contiguous SELL-block ordering. Its productive opening, late seed/fertilizer cuts, and queue compaction are inherited/composed around the same route bank; this is mainly market-ordering diversity rather than new production geometry.
novelty_ranking.use: Use only for final market-order sensitivity, not as a less-correlated production opponent.

novelty_conclusion: None of the three is a genuinely new production family relative to the repository. Population has the best production-level idea but is a semantic duplicate of the existing 2945 candidate; Cha22 and Soil retain the same shared 41-route payload and chiefly add or reorder wrapper layers.

entrypoint.intended_policy: ig_agent (queue-hole closure over the full cha20_entry_agent chain)
entrypoint.concern: The final global named agent remains the older E343 weed-lag wrapper from line 6182. Later layers update cha20_entry_agent and kaggle_agent but never rebind agent. A harness that imports main.agent silently omits ready-stock advancing, terminal liquidation, EarlyCycle, funding/economic filters, reorder, late-input caps, merge, and IG closure.
entrypoint.adapter_required: Yes for name-based harnesses: load with Kaggle get_last_callable semantics or externally bind the callable ig_agent as agent. Do not modify downloaded source.

candidates.production_mix: The common route bank mixes cows, sheep, geese, wheat, carrot, strawberry, and melon. The shipped suffix fixes _PIPE_MODE='EarlyCycle': it repurposes idle opening labor to plant/water an extra wheat, delays its harvest to a later day, restores the pasture, and delivers/sells the extra wheat. It also has visible-price carrot/herd substitutions inherited earlier in the chain and late seed/fertilizer caps.
candidates.route_adaptability: At day 6 it selects a shop-pair route, sending Yarn Store worlds to the older V39 routes and other shop pairs to EXP240 routes; at day 27 it forces route 2. It records a rival opening signature but the shipped router does not dispatch on that signature. Later wrappers react to visible prices, shops, stock, rival sales, weeds, and funding state.
policy_level_changes: Fixed EarlyCycle productive opening with one extra temporary wheat and delayed harvest/delivery.
Three-turn ready-stock sale advance, terminal seven-turn liquidation, multiple visible-state funding/economic filters, and final sale reorder/queue compaction.
Late fertilizer-use guard and remaining-plant-based wheat/carrot seed cap.
Same-item market-order merging followed by dead-sale hole closure.

comparison.assessment: Not cosmetic-only, because EarlyCycle and late input guards change physical production; nevertheless the trajectory bank and most production logic are inherited from the same large family, so correlation remains high.

Between steps 144-191, another bounded plan can replace planned cows/pastures with geese/coops only in no-milk/no-yarn shop worlds when the estimated gain clears both a 1.3 ratio and $600 threshold. comparison.assessment: The dynamic livestock substitution is genuine production geometry, but this notebook adds zero new strategy semantics and should be deduplicated against the existing 2945 candidate.
